channel.title: Threat Desk
channel.description: Vulnerabilities, advisories and threat activity, twice a day

item.title: Microsoft warns of potential printing failures for Forcepoint users after hotpatch
item.description: The November 2026 Windows hotpatch may cause Print Spooler failures on Windows 11 24H2 systems running Forcepoint DLP Endpoint Agent.

item.title: Peruvian call centre operator jailed for $15m government impersonation fraud
item.description: A Lima-based operator was sentenced to eight years for managing call centres that defrauded over 30,000 Spanish-speaking US residents.

item.title: NYSDFS settles $6.75m with Rocket Mortgage and Mr. Cooper
item.description: New York regulators announced settlements with two major mortgage lenders, highlighting the importance of effective multi-factor authentication controls and timely incident reporting.

item.title: Cyberattack disrupts Guadeloupe university hospital IT systems
item.description: A major cyberattack on Saturday night forced the Guadeloupe university hospital to activate its emergency response plan and postpone non-emergency procedures.

item.title: GlobeTopper loses $2.5m after API credential theft
item.description: A cyberattack on B2B gift card distributor GlobeTopper resulted in $2.5m in lost revenue and the redemption of $70,000 in digital gift cards.

item.title: LaLiga confirms cyberattack exposed fan personal data
item.description: Spain's top football league disclosed that a cybercriminal accessed its fan services platform between 14 and 16 November, extracting personal data from registered users.

item.title: RansomwareHelp CTO indicted for wire fraud after FBI sting
item.description: The co-founder of a firm claiming to decrypt ransomware without payment has been charged with wire fraud after an FBI operation revealed he was secretly paying attackers and charging victims a markup.

item.title: CISA adds MONAI Label and Mail Assure flaws to KEV Catalog
item.description: CISA has added two critical vulnerabilities to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities Catalog, citing active exploitation of a path traversal flaw in MONAI Label and an SSRF issue in N-able Mail Assure.

item.title: Verizon report: Credential abuse drives 13% of breaches
item.description: Verizon's 2026 Data Breach Investigations Report identifies credential abuse as the initial access vector in 13% of breaches.

item.title: Michigan nurse jailed for $1.6m Medicare fraud using stolen records
item.description: A home health care owner was sentenced to four years in prison for billing Medicare for services that were never performed, using stolen patient data.

item.title: Austrian Foreign Ministry website breached, diplomat contacts exposed
item.description: A breach of an external website exposed official contact details for Austrian diplomats, with no attribution yet made.

item.title: Human Security disrupts BadBox 3.0 ad fraud botnet
item.description: The third iteration of the BadBox operation generated 40 billion daily bid requests by spoofing CTV apps on low-cost Android devices.

item.title: Dragos finds prompt theft at three AI inference providers
item.description: Threat actors stole customer prompts and credentials from at least three AI inference providers, with none detecting the intrusions until notified by researchers.

item.title: Peninsula Energy warns of disruption after Wyoming cyber incident
item.description: An Australian-listed energy company has requested a trading halt to investigate a cybersecurity breach at its uranium project in Wyoming.

item.title: Tower Records cyberattack potentially leaks 11 million customer records
item.description: Japanese retailer Tower Records announced a cyberattack on 19 November 2026 potentially compromised 11 million customer records, including names, dates of birth and delivery addresses.

item.title: SOCRadar: AI agent used to target European banks
item.description: SOCRadar research identifies a French-speaking cybercriminal using a jailbroken AI agent to target European financial and municipal sectors.

item.title: KEPCO confirms breach exposing 1.5 million individuals
item.description: South Korea's main power utility confirmed a breach of its billing and procurement systems, exposing sensitive data for over 1.5 million individuals.

item.title: Riken suspends Fugaku supercomputer after external intrusion
item.description: Japan’s Riken institute has cut off external access to the Fugaku supercomputer after detecting suspicious traffic that allowed an outside party to tamper with internal servers.

item.title: NSA restores normal operations after PHP patching caused internal network outages
item.description: The US National Security Agency has returned to normal operations after patches to PHP caused disruptions to its internal classified communications network, NSANet, for three days.

item.title: House report warns US firms on Chinese open-weight AI risks
item.description: A joint congressional report urges US companies to stop embedding Chinese open-weight AI models, citing national security risks and the difficulty of removing such dependencies.

item.title: Kirsten Davies appointed US National Cyber Director
item.description: The Department of War CIO replaces Sean Cairncross as the new National Cyber Director.

item.title: FBI investigating apparent hack of National Crime Information Center
item.description: The FBI is investigating an apparent intrusion into the NCIC, a critical database used by law enforcement agencies nationwide, according to a person familiar with the matter.

item.title: CISA warns of active exploitation of SAP NetWeaver and Cisco Expressway flaws
item.description: CISA warned that threat actors are exploiting two vulnerabilities in the wild: one in SAP NetWeaver and one in Cisco Expressway devices.

item.title: GL.iNet patches remote management flaw exploited to deploy malware
item.description: A threat actor exploited a vulnerability in GL.iNet's GoodCloud platform to install malware on routers and KVM devices, prompting the vendor to recommend installing a security firmware update.

item.title: PHP patches phpAfterShell flaw enabling RCE via session corruption
item.description: PHP has released patches for CVE-2026-126714, a critical vulnerability that allows remote code execution by exploiting interrupted session writes to trigger object deserialization.

item.title: N-able patches critical SSRF flaw in Mail Assure
item.description: N-able has released a patch for a critical server-side request forgery vulnerability discovered during its investigation into a cyberattack on its Mail Assure and SpamExperts services.

item.title: Norwegian energy firms hit by Azure API Management flaw
item.description: Norway's NSM confirmed that Equinor and Skagerak Energi were targeted via a security issue in Azure API Management, which Microsoft has now patched.

item.title: Azure APIM flaw exploited to target Norwegian energy firms
item.description: Microsoft closed an access path in Azure API Management that allowed unauthorised access to secrets, impacting Equinor and Skagerak Energi.

item.title: Azure API Management flaw exploited to steal API credentials
item.description: Microsoft confirmed a vulnerability in Azure API Management Classic tiers was exploited to access stored secrets, with Norwegian authorities linking the incident to attacks on energy companies.

item.title: Cisco Expressway RCE added to CISA KEV
item.description: Cisco has released a fix for a critical remote code execution flaw in Expressway Series devices that CISA has listed as known exploited.
